title: Preventive Maintenance Agreements — Renewal, Escalation and Termination Terms by Tier
content:
## Contract administration terms table

The renewal mechanics and the termination figures of the Preventive Maintenance Agreements are fixed per tier as set out in this table.

| Tier | Renews automatically at the end of the term | Calendar days before term end at which the renewal window opens | Calendar days before term end by which a non-renewal notice must be received to stop an automatic renewal | Price escalation applied to the annual price at each renewal (percent) | Fee on the unbilled remainder of the term when the owner terminates for convenience (percent) | Calendar days of written notice before a termination for convenience takes effect |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Filter & Belt Service Plan | yes | 60 | 30 | 4.0 | 25 | 30 |
| Inspection Agreement | yes | 60 | 30 | 4.0 | 25 | 30 |
| Preventive Maintenance Agreement | yes | 90 | 30 | 3.5 | 25 | 30 |
| Labor Coverage Agreement | yes | 90 | 60 | 3.5 | 35 | 60 |
| Full Coverage Agreement | yes | 90 | 60 | 3.0 | 40 | 60 |
| Comprehensive Performance Agreement | no | 120 | 90 | 3.0 | 50 | 90 |

### Table notes

1. Every tier renews automatically except the Comprehensive Performance Agreement.
2. The renewal window opens 60 days before term end at the two entry tiers, 90 days at the three middle tiers and 120 days at the Comprehensive Performance Agreement.
3. The non-renewal notice deadline is 30 days before term end at the three lower tiers, 60 days at the Labor Coverage Agreement and the Full Coverage Agreement, and 90 days at the Comprehensive Performance Agreement.
4. Escalation at renewal is 4.0 percent at the two entry tiers, 3.5 percent at the Preventive Maintenance Agreement and the Labor Coverage Agreement, and 3.0 percent at the two upper tiers.
5. The early termination fee rate rises from 25 percent to 50 percent, and the termination notice period from 30 to 90 calendar days, tier by tier as shown.
